summary:
The Lunar Landing Site Decision Support System is an interactive platform designed to help space mission planners evaluate and compare potential lunar landing locations and mission dates. The system integrates astronomical ephemeris data from NASA/JPL Horizons with lunar elevation data from NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) to analyze the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to selected landing sites while accounting for terrain obstructions.
Users can select predefined landing locations or enter custom lunar coordinates, choose a mission date, and explore key indicators such as sunlight availability, Earth visibility, longest continuous darkness, and potential communication blackout periods. Results are presented through interactive timelines, terrain-aware visualizations, and side-by-side scenario comparisons.
By transforming complex astronomical and topographic data into accessible, actionable insights, our solution supports more informed landing site selection and mission scheduling. It is important because successful lunar exploration depends not only on where we land, but also on when we land.
